     8	/-!
     9	# The finite-stage Picard glue as a scheme over its field of definition
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue package already contains affine algebras over its final finite
    12	subextension `P.N.1`.  Their structure maps agree on overlaps, so they descend to the
    13	glued scheme.  This retains the finite-stage object over `Spec P.N.1`, which is the
    14	object-level input for the scalar-extension comparison with the separably closed atlas.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    29	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    31	
    32	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    33	
    34	set_option linter.style.setOption false
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- Projecting the dependent scalar towers from `P` requires a larger local synthesis budget.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure map from the finite-stage glued scheme to its field of definition. -/
    39	noncomputable def gluedMap
    40	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    41	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    42	    P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1) := by
    43	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    44	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    45	  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>
    46	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U
    47	  let B : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u :=
    48	    fun U V =>
    49	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V
    50	  let r : ∀ U V, A U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    51	    pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    52	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    53	  letI : ∀ U V, Algebra (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    54	    pic0FiniteStageAlgebraOfMap (r U V)
    55	  letI : ∀ U V, IsScalarTower P.N.1 (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    56	    pic0FiniteStageTowerOfMap (r U V)
    57	  let tau : ∀ U V, B V U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    58	    pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
    59	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    60	  fapply Multicoequalizer.desc
    61	  · intro U
    62	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U
    63	    exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U)))
    64	  · rintro ⟨U, V⟩
    65	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U V
    66	    change
    67	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A U) (B U V))) ≫
    68	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U))) =
    69	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau U V).toRingHom) ≫
    70	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A V) (B V U)))) ≫
    71	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A V)))
    72	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    73	    rw [Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    74	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    75	    congr 1

    78	      ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
    79	      AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, Category.assoc, RingHom.coe_coe]
    80	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A U) (B U V)]
    81	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A V) (B V U)]
    82	    exact (tau U V).commutes x |>.symm
    83	
    84	/-- The finite-stage Picard glue, retained over the finite field `P.N.1`. -/
    85	noncomputable def gluedOver
    86	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    87	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Over (Spec (.of P.N.1)) :=
    88	  Over.mk P.gluedMap

     9	/-!
    10	# Projective morphisms
    11	
    12	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    13	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    14	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    15	-/

    17	open CategoryTheory Limits
    18	
    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24	
    25	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    26	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    27	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    28	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    29	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    30	
    31	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    32	
    33	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    34	
    35	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    36	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    37	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    38	  letI : Finite n := hn
    39	  haveI := hi
    40	  rw [← hcomp]
    41	  infer_instance
    42	
    43	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    44	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    45	  haveI := h.isProper
    46	  inferInstance
    47	
    48	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    49	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    50	  haveI := h.isProper
    51	  inferInstance
    52	
    53	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    54	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    55	  haveI := h.isProper
    56	  inferInstance
    57	
    58	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    59	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    60	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    65	
    66	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    67	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    68	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    69	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    70	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    71	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    72	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    73	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    74	
    75	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
    76	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    77	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
    78	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    79	  letI : Finite n := hn
    80	  haveI := hi
    81	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
    82	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
    83	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    84	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
    85	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
    86	      have hbig : IsPullback
    87	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
    88	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
    89	        rw [h1, hcomp]
    90	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
    91	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
    92	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
    93	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip

    10	/-!
    11	# Finite subsets of irreducible algebraic groups lie in affine opens
    12	
    13	This file formalizes the irreducible, algebraically closed core of
    14	[Stacks, Lemma 39.8.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B7S). Translation
    15	turns one affine neighborhood of the identity into finitely many dense open
    16	subsets. Irreducibility gives a common closed point, and translating back gives
    17	one affine open containing the prescribed rational points.
    18	
    19	The final theorem applies this argument to arbitrary finite sets of topological
    20	points: local finite type over a field makes the scheme Jacobson, so each point
    21	specializes to a closed point. It deliberately does not assert the remaining
    22	arbitrary-field or reducible-component descent.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits
    30	open MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
    31	open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme

    35	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
    36	
    37	/-- Right translation by a rational point of a group scheme. -/
    38	noncomputable def rightMul (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    39	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ⟶ G :=
    40	  lift (𝟙 G) (toUnit G ≫ p) ≫ μ
    41	
    42	lemma comp_rightMul {G Z : Over (Spec (.of K))} [GrpObj G]
    43	    (x : Z ⟶ G) (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
    44	    x ≫ rightMul G p = x * (toUnit Z ≫ p) := by
    45	  rw [rightMul, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift, Category.comp_id, comp_toUnit_assoc,
    46	    CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    47	
    48	/-- Right translation is inverted by translation by the inverse point. -/
    49	noncomputable def rightMulIso (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    50	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ≅ G where
    51	  hom := rightMul G p
    52	  inv := rightMul G (p ≫ ι)
    53	  hom_inv_id := by
    54	    rw [comp_rightMul, rightMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    55	    change ((𝟙 G) * (toUnit G ≫ p)) * (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ = 𝟙 G
    56	    simp
    57	  inv_hom_id := by
    58	    rw [comp_rightMul, rightMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    59	    change ((𝟙 G) * (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹) * (toUnit G ≫ p) = 𝟙 G
    60	    simp
    61	
    62	/-- Left translation by a rational point of a group scheme. -/
    63	noncomputable def leftMul (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    64	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ⟶ G :=
    65	  lift (toUnit G ≫ p) (𝟙 G) ≫ μ

    67	lemma comp_leftMul {G Z : Over (Spec (.of K))} [GrpObj G]

    12	/-!
    13	# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for
    14	
    15	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
    16	subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
    17	of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
    18	on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
    19	written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
    20	quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
    21	hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
    22	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    23	
    24	This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` from the project's
    25	finite-projective-space notion `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective`; projectivity is
    26	the closed-immersion special case.  The chain is
    27	
    28	  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
    29	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
    30	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` H-quasi-projective over `S`.
    31	
    32	## The two avoidance inputs
    33	
    34	The original deep input is the first step, and it is **absent from mathlib
    35	`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
    36	`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
    37	of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
    38	produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
    39	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
    40	Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
    41	where the grading is consumed.
    42	
    43	For a closed immersion the final transport is cheap: `IsClosedImmersion →
    44	IsAffineHom`, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage` pulls affine opens back.  An open
    45	immersion needs a second prime-avoidance step: after placing the finite image in
    46	an affine open, `GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite` shrinks it to a
    47	basic open lying inside the immersion range.  The standard closed/open
    48	factorization then gives transport along every immersion.
    49	
    50	Thus graded avoidance is the new algebraic result in this file.  Open-immersion
    51	transport is the only additional substantive geometric step; its algebra is
    52	delegated to the already-landed finite prime-avoidance theorem.  The remaining
    53	H-quasi-projective and coproduct declarations are factorization and packaging.
    54	
    55	## What this does and does not buy
    56	
    57	It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
    58	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
    59	nothing in this project produces an H-quasi-projective witness for the relevant
    60	Picard component.  Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`;
    61	formalizing and transporting that source theorem remains open.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
    62	that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
    63	standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
    64	condition invented here.  Stated as
    65	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective` in §3.
    66	
    67	It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
    68	Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme
    69	(`Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective`), which is what
    70	`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean` had only for *affine* `X` and what the
    71	Albanese lane's `OrbitsInAffineOpen` had for no `X` at all.  Smooth proper
    72	geometrically integral curves **are** projective in this project
    73	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
    74	`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), so §3 fires at the curve itself with no
    75	hypothesis beyond its own binders.
    76	
    77	## What §5 is NOT: read this before consuming `PointedPicSharpRepProjective`
    78	
    79	§5 restates the seam's antecedent with `IsProjective` of the representing scheme in
    80	place of `FiniteInAffine`.  **That antecedent is refuted at the object it is about**,
    81	and the refutation is landed here as a theorem, not left as prose:
    82	`Scheme.not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.  Projectivity over a field

    85	**disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** (Kleiman §6 `ex:curves`), which is not quasi-compact.

    87	strictly stronger and false at `Pic_{C/k}`.

    90	a `P → Q` whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting", and it is caught by
    91	that file's own theorems.  Kleiman's `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`,
    92	not projectivity of the ambient scheme.  §5 therefore survives only as a
    93	*conditional* reduction with an explicitly refuted antecedent; §3 and §4, which do not
    94	mention the ambient Picard scheme, are unaffected.
    95	
    96	An earlier revision of this section said §5 states the seam "with no condition invented
    97	in this project anywhere in it".  Both halves were wrong: `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` is
    98	project-local (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`, mathlib `v4.31` has no

   102	though the Lean definition is ours.

     9	# Projective and H-quasi-projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	A morphism is **H-quasi-projective** when it factors through a quasi-compact
    16	immersion into such a projective space, following the finite-projective-space
    17	convention of [Stacks, Tag 01VV].  The quasi-compactness is part of the
    18	definition: without it the predicate only records an immersion/relative very
    19	ampleness and need not imply finite type.  This predicate is not asserted to
    20	be equivalent over arbitrary bases to every formulation using relative ample
    21	line bundles.  Both predicates are stable under base change.
    22	
    23	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    24	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    25	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    26	-/

    36	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    37	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    38	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    39	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    40	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    41	
    42	/-- A morphism is H-quasi-projective if it admits a quasi-compact immersion into
    43	a finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    44	def Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    45	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    46	    IsImmersion i ∧ QuasiCompact i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    47	
    48	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    49	
    50	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    51	
    52	/-- A projective morphism is H-quasi-projective. -/
    53	theorem isHQuasiProjective (h : pi.IsProjective) : pi.IsHQuasiProjective := by
    54	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    55	  letI : Finite n := hn
    56	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
    57	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, inferInstance, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
    58	
    59	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    60	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  rw [← hcomp]
    65	  infer_instance
    66	
    67	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    68	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    69	  haveI := h.isProper
    70	  inferInstance
    71	
    72	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    73	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    74	  haveI := h.isProper
    75	  inferInstance
    76	
    77	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    78	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    79	  haveI := h.isProper
    80	  inferInstance
    81	
    82	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    83	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    84	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    85	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    86	  letI : Finite n := hn
    87	  haveI := hi
    88	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    89	
    90	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    91	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    92	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    93	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    94	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    95	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    96	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    97	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    98	
    99	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   100	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   101	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
   102	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
   103	  letI : Finite n := hn
   104	  haveI := hi
   105	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
   106	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   107	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   108	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
   109	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   110	      have hbig : IsPullback
   111	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   112	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   113	        rw [h1, hcomp]
   114	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   115	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   116	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   117	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   118	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
   119	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   120	
   121	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective

   129	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, _, hcomp⟩ := h

   139	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi

   148	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi

   150	  infer_instance

   154	theorem comp_isImmersion (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
   155	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] :
   156	    (j ≫ pi).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   157	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   158	  letI : Finite n := hn
   159	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   160	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   161	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
   162	
   163	/-- The comparison from a base-changed source to the corresponding base change
   164	of its ambient projective space. -/
   165	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
   166	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :

   170	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
   171	
   172	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   173	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   174	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   175	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   176	  letI : Finite n := hn
   177	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   178	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   179	  have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   180	      pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   181	  have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)

   184	        (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))

   189	      (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   190	      (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   191	  exact ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp,
   192	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi,

   771	(`not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`).  The usable replacement is a
   772	coproduct of components that each carry an H-quasi-projective witness.  Constructing
   773	those component witnesses is a separate producer obligation.

   775	`FiniteInAffine`, unlike `IsProjective` or `CompactSpace`, **is** closed under such
   776	coproducts: a finite set meets only finitely many components, each hit in an affine open,
   777	and finitely many disjoint affine opens have an affine `iSup`
   778	(`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`).  So this section turns the refuted globally-projective
   779	antecedent into a degree-graded substrate — `FiniteInAffine` of the ambient coproduct
   780	follows from H-quasi-projectivity of each supplied component, which is exactly the
   781	geometric adapter a future degree assembly can consume.  This file does not construct
   782	that assembly or any Picard representer.
   783	
   784	Everything here is about coproducts of arbitrary schemes and carries **no** hypothesis
   785	about the curve; nothing closes the seam.  It is the substrate the earlier sections said
   786	was missing ("degree-invariance of the semilinear action, together with the degree-graded
   787	decomposition of `PicSchemeEt`" — the second half). -/

   789	section Coproduct

   791	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` is closed under arbitrary set-indexed coproducts.**  If every
   792	component scheme `g i` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, so does `∐ g`.

   794	A finite `s ⊆ ∐ g` meets only the finitely many components indexed by `idx '' s`; within

   796	affine open `U i`; the images `Sigma.ι g i ''ᵁ U i` are pairwise disjoint
   797	(`disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι`) affine opens (image of an affine open under an open
   798	immersion), so their finite `iSup` is affine (`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`) and
   799	contains `s`.

   802	scheme has and global projectivity does not. -/
   803	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] (g : σ → Scheme.{u})
   804	    (h : ∀ i, FiniteInAffine (g i)) : FiniteInAffine (∐ g) := by
   805	  classical
   806	  letI : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι g i) := fun i =>
   807	    Scheme.IsLocallyDirected.instIsOpenImmersionι (Discrete.functor g) { as := i }
   808	  intro s hs
   809	  have hcomp : ∀ x : (∐ g : Scheme.{u}), ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (Sigma.ι g i).base := by
   810	    intro x
   811	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := (sigmaOpenCover g).exists_eq x
   812	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
   813	  choose idx hidx using hcomp
   814	  have hpre : ∀ i : σ, ((Sigma.ι g i).base ⁻¹' s).Finite := fun i =>
   815	    hs.preimage ((Sigma.ι g i).isOpenEmbedding.injective).injOn
   816	  choose U hU using fun i => h i _ (hpre i)
   817	  set J : Set σ := idx '' s with hJ
   818	  have hJfin : J.Finite := hs.image idx
   819	  refine ⟨⟨⨆ i ∈ J, (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
   820	  · apply IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint hJfin
   821	    · intro i _
   822	      exact (U i).2.image_of_isOpenImmersion _
   823	    · intro i _ j _ hij
   824	      exact Disjoint.mono (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _)
   825	        (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _) (disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι g i j hij)
   826	  · intro x hx
   827	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hidx x
   828	    have hyU : y ∈ (U (idx x)).1 := by
   829	      apply hU (idx x)
   830	      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, hy]
   831	      exact hx
   832	    have hmem : x ∈ (Sigma.ι g (idx x)) ''ᵁ (U (idx x)).1 := ⟨y, hyU, hy⟩
   833	    exact (le_iSup₂ (f := fun i _ => (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1) (idx x)
   834	      ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩) hmem
   835	
   836	/-- A coproduct of schemes that are projective over one affine base satisfies
   837	`FiniteInAffine`. This is the degree-piece bridge: projectivity is checked on
   838	each component, while `FiniteInAffine` is concluded for their possibly infinite
   839	coproduct. -/
   840	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective
   841	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   842	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjective) :
   843	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   844	  finiteInAffine_sigma _ fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isProjective (hX i)
   845	
   846	/-- A coproduct of H-quasi-projective schemes over one affine base satisfies
   847	`FiniteInAffine`, even when the coproduct itself is not quasi-compact. -/
   848	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective
   849	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   850	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
   851	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   852	  finiteInAffine_sigma _ fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective (hX i)
   853	
   854	/-- The carried very-ample form of `finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective`.
   855	At `Scheme.{0}`, `IsProjectiveWith` records a line bundle together with its
   856	closed immersion into relative projective space; forgetting those certificates
   857	piecewise gives `FiniteInAffine` for the coproduct. -/
   858	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjectiveWith
   859	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   860	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   861	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   862	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   863	  finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective X fun i => (hX i).isProjective
   864	
   865	/-- The carried relatively very ample form of
   866	`finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective`. -/
   867	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjectiveWith
   868	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   869	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   870	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   871	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   872	  finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective X fun i =>
   873	    (hX i).isHQuasiProjective
   874	
   875	/-- A coproduct in `Over S` is locally of finite type when each of its
   876	components is. The proof compares its structure morphism with the descent
   877	morphism from the coproduct of the underlying schemes and uses that
   878	`LocallyOfFiniteType` is Zariski-local at the source. -/
   879	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_sigma
   880	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}}
   881	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (X i).hom) :
   882	    LocallyOfFiniteType (∐ X).hom := by

   894	  exact MorphismProperty.comp_mem @LocallyOfFiniteType
   895	    (PreservesCoproduct.iso (Over.forget S) X).hom
   896	    (Sigma.desc fun i => (X i).hom)
   897	    (by infer_instance)
   898	    (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) hX)
   899	
   900	/-- The underlying scheme of the canonical coproduct in `Over S` inherits
   901	`FiniteInAffine` from its components.  This comparison lemma is independent of
   902	projectivity and is the reusable coproduct boundary. -/
   903	theorem finiteInAffine_over_sigma
   904	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}}

   906	    FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=

   910	/-- The canonical coproduct in `Over S` satisfies `FiniteInAffine` when every

   912	degree-piece representability assembly; `Over.forget S` identifies its
   913	underlying scheme with the coproduct handled by

   917	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjective) :
   918	    FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   919	  finiteInAffine_over_sigma X fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isProjective (hX i)
   920	
   921	/-- The canonical coproduct in `Over S` satisfies `FiniteInAffine` when each
   922	component is H-quasi-projective over the affine base. -/
   923	theorem finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective
   924	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   925	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
   926	    FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   927	  finiteInAffine_over_sigma X fun i =>
   928	    finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective (hX i)
   929	
   930	/-- Very-ample projective degree pieces supply the two geometric side
   931	conditions required of their canonical coproduct by `PointedPicSharpRep`:
   932	local finite type of its structure morphism and `FiniteInAffine` of its
   933	underlying scheme. No representability hypothesis is introduced here. -/
   934	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_and_finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjectiveWith
   935	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   936	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   937	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   938	    LocallyOfFiniteType (∐ X).hom ∧ FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   939	  ⟨locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun i => (hX i).locallyOfFiniteType,
   940	    finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isProjective X fun i => (hX i).isProjective⟩
   941

   943	line bundles supply the two geometric side conditions for their canonical
   944	coproduct: local finite type and `FiniteInAffine`.  The theorem deliberately

   947	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_and_finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjectiveWith
   948	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   949	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)

   964	  cases i
   965	  · simpa using hX
   966	  · simpa using hY
   967	
   968	end Coproduct

1	/-

     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.GrpObjFoldSum
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action
    12	
    13	`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
    14	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
    15	needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
    16	stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
    17	quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
    18	`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    19	
    20	That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
    21	it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.
    22	
    23	## What was actually going on
    24	
    25	`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
    26	for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
    27	a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
    28	the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
    29	`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
    30	`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
    31	`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.
    32	
    33	So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
    34	data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
    35	generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
    36	copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
    37	being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
    38	direction that should go.
    39	
    40	## Main results
    41	
    42	* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
    43	  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
    44	* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
    45	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
    46	  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
    47	  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
    48	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` — **the `S_n` instantiation**: for `C` a `k̄`-scheme, every
    49	  point of `C^n` has an `S_n`-stable affine open neighbourhood, given the orbit hypothesis.
    50	
    51	**Correction (2026-07-29): the `S_n` producer exists and this file's scope note said it did
    52	not.** Two earlier revisions ran in opposite directions and both were wrong. One advertised a
    53	`permAction : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut (C^n)` that did not exist; the correction then
    54	recorded building it as blocked, on the grounds that `MonObj.permAut` "is a bare morphism
    55	never shown to be an isomorphism" and `SymPowColimit.permEnd` "lands in `End`, not `Aut`".
    56	Both grounds were accurate statements about the tree and the inference from them was not:
    57	`permAut C σ⁻¹` is a two-sided inverse of `permAut C σ`, because
    58	`permAut C σ ≫ permAut C τ = permAut C (σ * τ)`. That is `MonObj.permAut_comp`, and the
    59	action is `MonObj.permAutHom`, both now in `Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean` — four lines, no
    60	construction. The lesson is the `permEnd` convention: the inverse `permEnd` carries is forced
    61	by `End`'s reversed multiplication, and reading it as a fact about `permAut` is what made an
    62	isomorphism look absent.
    63	
    64	## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis
    65	
    66	The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
    67	characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
    68	`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
    69	through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.
    70	
    71	## Scope — what this does and does not give
    72	
    73	**Does**: prove the stable-cover statement at the generality a glue-data construction wants —
    74	a *finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms*, with no Galois hypothesis and no
    75	characteristic hypothesis.
    76	
    77	**Does** now also apply it to `S_n` acting on `C^n`: `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` for the
    78	product in `Scheme`, and `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm_over` for the underlying scheme of the
    79	`Over (Spec k̄)`-product — **which is the one the leg uses**, and is a different object (see
    80	that theorem's docstring; `Over.forget` does not preserve binary products).
    81	
    82	**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open and
    83	`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged.
    84	
    85	**The count, in one place, because three places in this tree disagreed about it.** A glue-data
    86	assembly needs *four* things:
    87	
    88	1. ✓ a `G`-stable affine cover — below, with both `S_n` instantiations.
    89	2. ✓ the `Aut`-valued `S_n`-action — `MonObj.permAutHom` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`).
    90	3. ✓ **(completed run 0069 r7; this entry read "Partly" until then.)** The `n`-ary coproduct of
    91	   commutative algebras = `n`-fold tensor power, with the permutation action matched to
    92	   `PiTensorProduct.permAlgHom`. The algebra level is `Albanese/TensorPowerCoproduct.lean`
    93	   (`existsUnique_coprodLift`, `coprodLift_permAlgHom`, `permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom`); the
    94	   `Cofan`/`IsColimit` packaging in `Under k` that was the missing half is
    95	   `Albanese/TensorPowerCofan.lean` (`tensorPowerCofanIsColimit`, with
    96	   `tensorPowerFanIsLimit` for the `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` variance and
    97	   `tensorPowerCofan_inj_permAlgHom` for the equivariance on coprojections).
    98	4. **Open, and the honest wall.** The cocycle/overlap agreement of the chart quotients, plus
    99	   `OrbitsInAffineOpen` **for the curve** — where quasi-projectivity would enter, and mathlib
   100	   has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin.
   101

The existing infrastructure gives an axiom-clean orbit-affineness instance as soon as projectivity of the finite-stage glued morphism is available. No edits were made.

**Minimal Rebuild Chain**

In [FiniteInAffine.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/FiniteInAffine.lean:32):

```lean
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
```

At line 66:

```lean
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    (h : Scheme.FiniteInAffine X) :
    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen
```

This file imports:

```lean
AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.SemilinearAction
Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Affine
```

In [QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean:64):

```lean
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isProjective
    [IsAffine S] {π : X ⟶ S} (h : π.IsProjective) :
    Scheme.FiniteInAffine X
```

Thus, for `ρ` on a glued finite-stage object:

```lean
letI : ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen :=
  Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine ρ
    (Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isProjective hproj)
```

where `hproj : P.gluedMap.IsProjective`. The needed imports are:

```lean
AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine
AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteGaloisRepresentable
```

The convenience theorem already present in the original project, but not Rebuild, is [QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean:516):

```lean
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective
    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    [IsAffine S] {π : X ⟶ S} (h : π.IsProjective) :
    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen
```

It is just the two-theorem composition above.

**Orbit Infrastructure**

The class is [SemilinearAction.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/SemilinearAction.lean:141):

```lean
class SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
    ∃ U : X.affineOpens,
      ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom.base x ∈ U.1
```

Consumers:

- `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`, [StableAffineCover.lean:200](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/StableAffineCover.lean:200).
- `hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`, [StableAffineCover.lean:287](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/StableAffineCover.lean:287).
- `StableAffineOpen.hasGaloisQuotient_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`, [GaloisQuotientOverlap.lean:1635](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GaloisQuotientOverlap.lean:1635).
- `instOrbitsInAffineOpen_of_isAffine` and `instOrbitsInAffineOpen_pullback`, [GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean:95](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean:95) and line 135.

The Picard descent consumer is [Pic0FiniteGaloisRepresentable.lean:35](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteGaloisRepresentable.lean:35), whose `pic0RepresentableBy_finiteGaloisDescent` requires:

```lean
[((pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep).OrbitsInAffineOpen)]
```

**Other FiniteInAffine Producers**

Rebuild has:

- `finiteInAffine_of_isAffine`, `finiteInAffine_of_iso`, `finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom`, and `finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom` in `Descent/FiniteInAffine.lean`, lines 36, 41, 51, 58.
- `finiteInAffine_of_isOpenImmersion`, `finiteInAffine_of_isImmersion`, `finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace`, and `finiteInAffine_of_isProjective` in `Descent/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean`, lines 26, 44, 55, 64.
- `finiteInAffine_proj`, `finiteInAffine_p1`, `finiteInAffine_left_of_isFinite_toP1`, and `finiteInAffine_relCurve_of_isFinite_toP1` in [RelativeCurveFiniteInAffine.lean:169](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RelativeCurveFiniteInAffine.lean:169).
- `GroupScheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible` in [GroupAffineOpen.lean:162](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GroupAffineOpen.lean:162).

The group-scheme route requires `[IsAlgClosed K]`, `[LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom]`, and `[IrreducibleSpace G.left]`; it does not apply to a general finite Galois stage.

The original project additionally has:

- `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective` in [ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean:44](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean:44).
- `finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective` and `finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjectiveWith` in [QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean:484](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean:484).
- Open-subscheme variants at lines 728, 747, 758 and sigma/coproduct variants at lines 803-959.

Rebuild currently has no matching `IsHQuasiProjective` declaration.

**Blocking Gap**

`Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage.gluedMap` is defined in [Pic0FiniteStageGluedOver.lean:39](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageGluedOver.lean:39), and `gluedOver` at line 85. There is currently no theorem proving any of:

```lean
P.gluedMap.IsProjective
P.gluedMap.IsHQuasiProjective
Scheme.FiniteInAffine P.glueData.glued
```

Nor is there a general theorem descending `FiniteInAffine` from a faithfully flat field base change. The existing base-change files only provide chart/gluing comparison isomorphisms, not the global geometric property. Therefore the orbit instance is immediately obtainable from a new projectivity witness, but existing declarations alone do not yet produce it for `P.gluedOver`.

`#print axioms`/LSP verification for the relevant projectivity, `FiniteInAffine`, and orbit theorems reports only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`; there are no project-specific axioms in this chain.

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`). Before working on a graph node,
  inspect its tags and any `TO CHECK` reason; `TO CHECK` is an attention marker,
  not a mathematical verdict.
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGlueDataAssembly
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageTransitionModels
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModels

/-!
# An inhabited finite-stage Picard glue package

The simultaneous pair- and triple-transition descent theorems supply every input of
`pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData`.  This file records those dependent inputs in one
package and immediately exposes the resulting scheme glue datum.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
-- The fields retain three nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
/-- All finite-stage models and comparison equations needed to assemble the descended
Picard atlas.  The fields are outputs of the simultaneous finite-subextension producers,
not additional geometric hypotheses. -/
structure Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] where
  L : DatG0.FinSubext F k
  n : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
  m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
  relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1
  e : forall j,
    k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
      Pic0FiniteStageRing C j
  M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k
  mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
        (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
      Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)
  hmapM : forall q,
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
        (AlgHom.id L.1
          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
        ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
        L.1).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
          (AlgHom.id L.1
            (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
              (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
              (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
              (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))
  hOpen : forall i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
    IsOpenImmersion
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))
  N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k
  thetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
        C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
        C L n m relation M mapM p
  hthetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
        (AlgHom.id M.1
          (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
            C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
        ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
        C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
          M.1).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
          (AlgHom.id M.1
            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
              C L n m relation M mapM p)))

namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

set_option maxHeartbeats 25600000 in
-- The package projections retain the dependent tensor-product instances of the constructor.
/-- The scheme glue datum computed from an inhabited finite-stage package. -/
noncomputable def glueData
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Scheme.GlueData := by
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
  exact pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData
    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N
      P.e P.hmapM P.hOpen P.thetaN P.hthetaN

end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
-- Selecting both finite families exposes many dependent quotient-algebra instances.
set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
/-- The simultaneous finite-stage descent producers inhabit the glue package. -/
theorem exists_pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] :
    Nonempty (Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨L, n, m, relation, e, M, mapM, hmapM, hOpen, _⟩ :=
    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTransition_models (C := C) (F := F)
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic L.1 k := by infer_instance
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k := by infer_instance
  let Q := pic0FiniteStageTripleModelComparisonFamily
    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ :=
    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTripleTransition_models_of_comparisons
      C L n m relation M mapM Q
  choose thetaN hthetaN using hN
  exact ⟨{
    L := L
    n := n
    m := m
    relation := relation
    e := e
    M := M
    mapM := mapM
    hmapM := hmapM
    hOpen := hOpen
    N := N
    thetaN := thetaN
    hthetaN := by
      intro p
      simpa only [Q, pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels] using
        hthetaN p
  }⟩

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

/-!
# The finite-stage Picard glue as a scheme over its field of definition

The finite-stage glue package already contains affine algebras over its final finite
subextension `P.N.1`.  Their structure maps agree on overlaps, so they descend to the
glued scheme.  This retains the finite-stage object over `Spec P.N.1`, which is the

/-- The structure map from the finite-stage glued scheme to its field of definition. -/
noncomputable def gluedMap
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1) := by
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>
    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U
  let B : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u :=
    fun U V =>
      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V
  let r : ∀ U V, A U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
  letI : ∀ U V, Algebra (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    pic0FiniteStageAlgebraOfMap (r U V)
  letI : ∀ U V, IsScalarTower P.N.1 (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    pic0FiniteStageTowerOfMap (r U V)
  let tau : ∀ U V, B V U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
  fapply Multicoequalizer.desc
  · intro U
    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U
    exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U)))
  · rintro ⟨U, V⟩
    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U V
    change
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A U) (B U V))) ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U))) =
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau U V).toRingHom) ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A V) (B V U)))) ≫
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A V)))
    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    rw [Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    congr 1
    ext x
    simp only [CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
      ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
      AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, Category.assoc, RingHom.coe_coe]
    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A U) (B U V)]
    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A V) (B V U)]
    exact (tau U V).commutes x |>.symm

/-- The finite-stage Picard glue, retained over the finite field `P.N.1`. -/
noncomputable def gluedOver
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Over (Spec (.of P.N.1)) :=
  Over.mk P.gluedMap
